properties.description:
`--ephemeral` serves a design that lives only in the process and is gone when it stops. Built to answer dec:idea-is-the-byte-backend-selectable-at-runtime, and shaped by it: named for what happens to the WORK rather than for which engine is underneath, because reflow2's premise is that a design outlives the session and a neutral `--backend memory` would frame durability as a preference.

REFUSES, rather than warns, alongside --graph-path, --registry-root, --shared and --serve-shared — each names a design on disk and the combination is likelier a mistake than an intention. --graph-path is detected from the ARGUMENTS, because a parsed value cannot tell a user's choice from clap's default.

SAYS SO IN THE HANDSHAKE, FIRST, because an agent connecting over HTTP never sees the operator's stderr. The condition is `graph_path: None` — the same fact as "no directory backs this" rather than a second flag that could drift — and it survives `share()`, so every per-session service carries it.

--export-to still works, so a scratch design can be written through to a file after all.
properties.name: A design can be served in memory only, labelled as scratch, and every flag that names a design on disk is refused alongside it
